NO release is dependent on char particle size and that NO reduction reactions are strongly temperature dependent.
the NO release from biomass char particles increases significantly during conversion, and this is due to an increased fraction of char N which is released as NO during conversion.
the NO release from char particles increases with time and is a function of the char particle diameter, temperature, and the char N content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model for the NO formation from char particles.
the development of new and more efficient methods for the production of energy from biomass.
the NO release from biomass char particles during combustion and the influence of char N content and the char conversion rate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the NO release from char combustion of biomass particles is strongly dependent on the particle size and the combustion conditions, and that NO reduction reactions are very important in determining the final NO emission.
the char N is released from biomass particles as NO in a time dependent manner.
the NO release rate from biomass char particles can be modeled with good accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NO release rate from char combustion of single particles can be modeled by assuming that char N is oxidized to NO in proportion to the experimental carbon oxidation rate.
NO formation from biomass combustion is mainly controlled by the amount of N released from the biomass and the reduction of NO to N2.
NO formation during biomass char combustion is controlled by the char N content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NO release rate is a complex function of particle size, conversion, and char N content.
the NO release from biomass chars is time dependent.
the NO release from biomass char particles cannot be neglected in the combustion of biomass.
